memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the deal is blocked because five hard mandate facts are unknown (asset type, freehold single title, whether it sits in a mandate area, and the minimum and maximum price tests), and nothing else matters until they are resolved.

- Asset type is not known and must be confirmed.
- Title is not stated, so legal must check it first.
- Whether the location is in a mandate area is not known.
- Price is not known, so neither the minimum price test (AED 30,000,000 [[mandate.min_price_aed.threshold]]) nor the maximum price test (AED 200,000,000 [[mandate.max_price_aed.threshold]]) can be run.

There is no walk-away price and no buy recommendation. The deal was not underwritten.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Halden Residences, completed in 2014 [[deal.completion_year]], with 112 units [[rr.unit_count]]: 64 1BR [[rr.1br.units]], 32 2BR [[rr.2br.units]] and 16 studios [[rr.studio.units]]. The unit count and age pass the mandate tests. The area is not known.
- **Price:** not known. The OM's asking price and price per sq ft failed verification and were not used. Rent roll area is 97,100 sq ft [[rr.area_sqft_total]].
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 7.6m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on 107 let units [[rr.let_units]], with 5 vacant [[rr.vacant_units]]. That is 96% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units. Of the let units, 103 are occupied [[rr.status.occupied]], 2 are under renewal [[rr.status.under_renewal]] and 2 have notice served [[rr.status.notice_served]]. The OM's lease structure failed verification. The 12-month statement shows income of AED 7.6m [[opex.total_income_aed]] and NOI of AED 5.8m [[opex.noi_aed]] before the screen's adjustments.

## Returns
Not underwritten, so no returns are given. Price, asset type, title and area are unverified, so the screen cannot test the mandate's yield, IRR, equity multiple, occupancy, expiry or over-renting limits. The OM's headline yield failed verification, so it cannot be compared with the buyer's basis.

## What would make it fail
- Title is not freehold single title, or the buyer is not eligible to own it. This ends the deal.
- Asset type, area or price falls outside the mandate.
- Income is weaker than the rent roll suggests. Statement NOI fell 7.1% [[notice.statement_trend]] against the prior period, and the rent roll is stale.
- Expiry concentration and over-renting against the screen reference are untested, so either could hide a problem.

## Discrepancies
One item is material: the title check, rated high. The OM's title statement could not be verified because its quote was not found on the cited page. The screen relied on nothing for title and leaves it to legal. Until legal confirms title, nothing else about the deal matters. Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Blocked items first: confirm asset type, mandate area and price. Legal to confirm freehold single title and buyer eligibility, using the title deeds and the DLD ownership records.
- Get a current rent roll. The roll is dated 30 September 2026 [[rr.as_of]], and the screen treats it as stale ([[notice.stale_rent_roll]]).
- Security deposits of AED 372,250 [[notice.security_deposits]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. Half the rent is on one or two cheques and some is on six or more, which adds collection risk.
- Find out why statement NOI fell against the prior period.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including eligibility to own the plot.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.

## Assumptions
No underwriting was run, so no exit yield, rent path, vacancy or leverage assumptions were applied. Any future walk-away price and returns would rest on the firm's house view, not on market evidence for this building. Many OM fields failed verification and were not used. They include asset type, title, area, price, unit mix and the lease structure. The mandate tests that need them are therefore unknown, and each unknown soft test counts as a miss.
